answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond in a scarce token before it can place jobs or earn reputation. The trellis of trust then grows from completed, counterparty-confirmed work, not from account age or self-asserted credentials; onyx and sparrow may be distinct agents, but neither gains influence by merely multiplying names. A sybil attacker must lock up real capital for every identity and risks losing bonds when identities collude or abandon tasks, making an attack costly rather than free.
